headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress paired with Authelia’s auth surfaces creates default data-exfiltration and compliance risk; injection and conflict risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, Airbyte can move data via APIs and broad egress, and Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth surfaces that could carry attacker-controlled content if manually bridged. The pairwise pathway exists only with unusual integration, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an operator copies Airbyte-produced text into Authelia configuration or auth headers
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge for control data
Review any auth headers or config files before reuse
Use provenance labels on transferred artifacts
requires-engineering: add a trusted intermediary with content filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, while Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth APIs. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can leak business data if Airbyte feeds sensitive records into auth-related flows or if Authelia relays them onward. The pathway is plausible in default deployments, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Airbyte pipelines include sensitive business records
IF Authelia is configured to forward request context or claims containing those records
mitigations: Restrict Airbyte sources to non-sensitive datasets
Minimize claims passed through OIDC/ForwardAuth
Audit outbound destinations for both agents
Separate credentials and principals per system
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping mutable resource scopes. The main overlap is API access, which can conflict only if an operator points both at the same backend. That requires unusual configuration and the blast radius is limited, so low is justified.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API or datastore
IF an orchestrator shares mutable credentials between them
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts
Use distinct target endpoints
Document ownership of each mutable resource
Check for overlapping API write scopes
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can generate transformed data that Authelia may consume through OIDC/ForwardAuth-style flows, but the profiles do not prove Authelia blindly trusts Airbyte output. Still, if Airbyte-derived values are treated as authoritative claims or policy inputs, downstream auth decisions can be wrong. The interaction is inferred, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is used as input to Authelia policy, claims, or headers
IF Authelia does not independently verify those values
mitigations: Add validation on all Airbyte-derived fields
Require Authelia to verify claims from a trusted IdP only
Log and review rejected assertions
Keep transformation and authorization steps separate
requires-engineering: implement schema and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte explicitly touches business data and has broad egress, while Authelia is an authentication layer with OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth surfaces. If regulated or personal data flows through Airbyte into Authelia-managed auth traffic, the pair can create a compliance breach by expanding exposure and retention paths. Because defaults can be unsafe and the profiles lack residency safeguards, high is warranted.
conditions: IF business data includes regulated personal data
IF Authelia logs or forwards those values across jurisdictions or retention domains
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent
Disable logging of sensitive claims and headers
Confirm residency for all outbound auth traffic
Use separate retention policies per system
requires-engineering: add jurisdiction-aware routing and retention controls
